output.summary: The deterministic overall policy verdict is NO_VERDICT (run validity VALID). The reference window (1704067200000–1704067320000) passed both business and resource policies (PASS), but the workload-01 window (1704067320000–1704067500000) has resource_verdict NO_VERDICT because the database-limit policy check on system-db-work returned NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS (10 of 180 expected cells missing, RESOURCE_GAPS). Business latency policy passed in both windows (response_time_p95_ms = 68 ≤ 200) and zero errors were recorded, but these do not convert the NO_VERDICT to PASS. All 9 resource-versus-latency correlation pairs in workload-01 are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED (constant control and constant series), all 5 anomaly checks report NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE with ZERO_MAD, and clock alignment is not verified by core. Analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS).

hypotheses.observation: The workload-01 resource policy check for rule database-limit on series system-db-work returned status NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, and the workload-01 window policy summary has resource_verdict NO_VERDICT and verdict NO_VERDICT; the system-db-work series in workload-01 has 10 missing cells out of 180 expected (observed 170), with reason RESOURCE_GAPS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The overall NO_VERDICT is plausibly caused by incomplete system-db-work telemetry during part of the workload-01 window, which prevented the database-limit rule from being evaluated; the evidence does not say why the cells are missing.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the collection pipeline for system-db-work over 1704067320000–1704067500000 to identify why 10 cells were not captured, then rerun (or otherwise complete the telemetry) so the database-limit rule can be evaluated.

hypotheses.observation: All 9 correlation pairs in workload-01 have status INSUFFICIENT_DATA with reasons including CONSTANT_CONTROL, NO_RANK_VARIATION, NO_RESIDUAL_VARIATION, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM and LOAD_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM, with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; the target-request-rate control was requested but dropped in every pair, and target_rate was constant at 80 requests/s with generator request_starts constant at 80 requests/s.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The workload had no load variation and the resource series were effectively constant, so the correlation method had no variation from which to estimate lag or rho; this is a design/coverage limitation, not evidence about whether load affects latency.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with a varying target-rate profile to create rank variation, then re-evaluate the association pairs; treat current results as NOT_ESTIMATED.

hypotheses.observation: All 5 anomaly checks in workload-01 report status NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE with episodes_reported 0 and reason ZERO_MAD; the diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested 5, episodes_reported 0, pairs_evaluable 0, and uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The reference series have zero MAD, so the detection method could not measure deviation from reference; the absence of reported episodes reflects a detection limitation on zero-variance series rather than demonstrated stability.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Provide a non-degenerate reference window or use a detection method that can evaluate zero-variance series before concluding the workload was stable.

hypotheses.observation: The resource binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, and the correlation pairs report LAG_NOT_EVALUABLE with best_lag_ms 0 and an empty lag_profile.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment between data sources, any temporal ordering or lead/lag interpretation would be unsupported; best_lag_ms 0 with an empty lag profile is not an established lag.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization across the load generator, service, and telemetry collectors before using any lag-based results.

hypotheses.observation: The overall latency policy check passed in both windows (response_time_p95_ms observed 68, threshold 200) and the overall metric summary shows 0 errors in 24000 samples, yet the overall policy verdict is NO_VERDICT.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The NO_VERDICT is attributable to incomplete resource coverage (missing database work cells), not to any observed application error; healthy-looking latency metrics do not turn a NO_VERDICT into PASS under product rules.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Keep the verdict as NO_VERDICT and complete the resource telemetry and rerun before considering the run acceptable; do not infer PASS from latency and error metrics alone.

recommendations.action: Complete the system-db-work telemetry for workload-01 (1704067320000–1704067500000) and rerun so the database-limit resource rule can be evaluated.
recommendations.rationale: The workload-01 resource verdict (and therefore the overall verdict) is NO_VERDICT strictly because the database-limit check on system-db-work had MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS; until that rule can be evaluated the window cannot receive PASS/FAIL.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment across the load generator, service, and any telemetry collectors before interpreting lag or temporal order in this run.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding explicitly reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, and all correlation lag profiles are not evaluable; temporal-causal conclusions would be unsupported without verified clocks.

recommendations.action: Rerun the association analysis with a varying target-rate profile instead of a constant 80 requests/s.
recommendations.rationale: All 9 correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with CONSTANT_CONTROL, NO_RANK_VARIATION, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM and LOAD_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM; load variation is required to estimate resource-versus-latency association.

recommendations.action: Inspect the telemetry/collection path that produced RESOURCE_GAPS and dropped 10 system-db-work cells in workload-01 (for example, collector restarts or extraction issues) rather than assuming a service-side cause.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence shows 10 of 180 expected cells missing for system-db-work in workload-01 and reason RESOURCE_GAPS, but it does not say why; a telemetry gap is one test-operator-addressable explanation.

recommendations.action: Do not cite the NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE anomaly results or the zero-error counts as proof of stability or absence of problems; treat association uncertainty as NOT_ESTIMATED.
recommendations.rationale: All anomaly checks used reference series with ZERO_MAD and reported episodes 0, and the diagnostic summary reports pairs_evaluable 0 with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; flat series and zero errors do not demonstrate stability or spare capacity.

caveats: The deterministic overall verdict is NO_VERDICT; this advisory does not change it. Only a rule the product can evaluate yields PASS or FAIL, and the workload-01 resource verdict stays NO_VERDICT until the missing-telemetry limitation is resolved.
Analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (reasons RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS) due to the 10 missing system-db-work cells in workload-01.
Clock alignment is not verified by core, so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypothesis is supported. Raw epoch values such as 1704067200000 are timestamps, not durations.

All 9 correlation pairs and all 5 anomaly checks in workload-01 have uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED or INSUFFICIENT_DATA; constant series and ZERO_MAD mean the absence of reported episodes/correlations does not prove absence of association or instability.
The PASS verdict for the reference window applies only to 1704067200000–1704067320000; it does not extend to workload-01 or the overall run.

Counts are scoped: the overall 24000 samples partition into 9600 (reference) and 14400 (workload-01); per-window and per-transaction counts are different quantities and should not be compared across scopes.
Latency summaries are constant 68 ms for p50/p95/p99/max in both windows and overall; per-sample variation, if any, cannot be inferred from these summary statistics alone.
The evidence contains no capacity bound, knee detector, or generator diagnostic guard data, so no conclusions about capacity limits or generator-health are possible from this input.
